title: Unfiltered ask heap and probe checklist — Jun 2027
content:
Purpose: scratchpad for the messy pile of customer asks collected from Q2 demos, support threads, and SRE postmortems. This is intentionally unfiltered — capture the ask, example signal, rough impact, and a 1–2 line probe we can run in a week. Use this to seed small experiments (engineer + CS pairing) and to push high-noise asks into product triage later.

Topline context and constraints:
- Volume: ~63 unique asks flagged between 2027-05-01 and 2027-06-10 across priority accounts (enterprise + fast-growth startups). Many duplicates and variations; this doc groups by behavioural theme not verbatim.
- Bias: heavy toward Dedicated/Private customers and performance-sensitive flows (low-latency chat, embeddings). Hosted-api voices under-sampled because they file tickets separately.
- Aim: identify 8 micro-probes (<=5 engineer-days) and 3 synthesis items for Product backlog.

Raw clusters (short labels + example):
1) Token accounting mismatch (billing visibility) — example: "customer A sees spike in tokens for prompt truncation and isn't sure which model caused it". Signal: billing disputes x3, Slack dm. Pain: high (invoicing risk).
2) Fallback artifacts in multi-model routing — example: fallback model returns shorter, truncated responses that break client parsing. Signal: integration test flakiness, SRE alert. Pain: medium-high.
3) Embedding drift at scale — example: same dataset re-embedding after model upgrade shows scoring shifts >20% for similarity thresholds. Signal: customer evals failed, internal eval run flagged. Pain: high for semantic search customers.
4) Slow cold-start for large context windows on Dedicated — example: warmup latency 800ms for first request with 16k tokens. Signal: dedicated pool perf logs. Pain: medium.
5) Missing audit log rows for private deployments (edge case) — example: some function-calls not recorded when customer uses external KMS. Signal: support ticket + compliance ask. Pain: high for regulated customers.
6) Inconsistent streaming chunk shapes across SDKs — example: Python SDK splits paragraphs differently than JS -> client rendering stutters. Signal: front-end bug + customer repro. Pain: low-medium.

Quick probe lane suggestions (1 paragraph per probe: objective, owner, success metric, rough steps):
- Probe 1 — Billing token delta explorer (owner: Amrita)
  Objective: give CS + customer a single page that reconciles tokens by request id, model, and truncation flag so we can quickly resolve invoice disputes.
  Success: reconciling 5 recent disputes in <48h; drop ticket escalations by 30%.
  Steps: minimal UI in Console (mock table) + backend query template; cache common queries. 2 engineer-days + 1 CS day. JIRA: CS-4128.

- Probe 2 — Fallback response emulation harness (owner: Daniel)
  Objective: reproduce fallback routing response shapes in a local harness so solutions engineers can validate client parsing.
  Success: build harness that caught 2 regression cases that previously hit production.
  Steps: small testbed to simulate routing rules + model variant substitutions. 3 engineer-days. Link: GH PR #2134.

- Probe 3 — Embedding consistency smoke (owner: Liam)
  Objective: run a canned dataset through candidate embedding model changes and produce a compact report showing pairwise rank correlation and threshold drift.
  Success: automated report created; a flag when drift > 10% over baseline.
  Steps: reuse existing eval runner, add a post-processing panel, surface in Console/Email. 4 engineer-days + 1 analyst day.

- Probe 4 — Cold-start warmup recipe (owner: Eng-on-call / SRE)
  Objective: create a startup warmup that pre-populates KV cache for common token prefixes and measure latency improvement.
  Success: reduce cold-start p50 by >=200ms on 16k sequences in dedicated env.
  Steps: script to run synthetic prefixes, monitor latency; deploy to one canary pool. 3 engineer-days.

- Probe 5 — Audit log KMS trace (owner: Security eng)
  Objective: reproduce missing audit rows with KMS enabled; add diagnostic flags to log KMS flow.
  Success: root cause identified and patch PR produced.
  Steps: replicate with customer config, add extra logging, coordinate with customer. 2-4 days.

- Probe 6 — Streaming normalize shim (owner: DevX)
  Objective: add a lightweight normalization layer in SDK streaming so chunk boundaries are consistent across languages (opt-in).
  Success: customers report smoother rendering; integration tests green.
  Steps: prototype in Python + JS, publish beta. 3 engineer-days.

- Probe 7 — Quick FAQ + template for "model upgrade embedding drift" (owner: CS writer)
  Objective: give customers a triage path and quick rollback template when embedding drift is detected.
  Success: decrease escalations to Eng from embedding drift threads by 40%.
  Steps: compile steps, example queries, regression alert thresholds; publish in Customer Docs. 1 day.

- Probe 8 — Low-effort telemetry flag (owner: SRE/infra)
  Objective: add a one-line flag to capture sequence-length histograms for failing requests for 48h windows to help debug perf anomalies.
  Success: first-usecase helps debug investigation within 24h.
  Steps: small telemetry patch + rollout to canary. 2 days.

Triage checklist (for each ask):
- Is it reproducible by CS? -> quick repro attached? (Y/N)
- Impact (revenue/regulatory/high-scale) -> H/M/L
- Required scope (console change / runtime change / SDK / infra)
- Quick probe candidate? (yes/no) + owner
- Linked artifacts (ticket / log snippets / sample request id)

Sample customer quotes (verbatim fragments collected):
- "We can't trust embeddings after the upgrade; thresholds moved and search results degrade." (security-saas customer)
- "Invoice is wrong — looks like the old model tokens are still billed even after we pinned version." (enterprise finance lead)
- "When model falls back, our webhook parser fails — it expects the same function schema." (marketplace partner)

Known unknowns / open questions:
- How much of embedding drift is due to floating-point differences vs model-param changes? Need quick experiment.
- Can Console feasibly show token-by-request without blowing up cost? What's the retention window we can realistically support?
- Is SDK normalization opt-in only (to avoid changing contract)? Preferred by customers?

Immediate next steps (this week):
- Owners above to confirm feasibility by 2027-06-22 (quick sync).
- Amrita to spin up Billing token delta mock and attach sample ticket (CS-4128).
- Liam to run one-shot embedding consistency report for account AcmeRetail using last-7-days snapshots.
- Sofia to compile a 1-page executive note for Product with top-3 candidate probes and ask for 2 dedicated engineer-days for quick wins.

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep this doc as cheap capture — we don't need final wording. Move anything we prototype into product backlog with a short PRD (1–2 pages).
- Lean on SEs for reproduction; their time is scarce so make repros tiny.
- When in doubt, prioritize items that reduce billing disputes and compliance risk first.

Appendix (quick pointers and refs):
- Repro query template: (paste in console) -> select requests where bill_amount_delta > 0.1 and truncation_flag = true; include model, request_id, account_id.
- Useful tickets: CS-4128 (invoice dispute), CS-4199 (fallback parsing error), SRE-773 (cold-start regression).

-- end of notes --
